context.why: Once a wording is in force, 'who approved this?' is the first question anybody asks, and nothing answers it today. This story makes each version keep who published it, frozen with the rest of the version, shown in the admin, and still honest after that account is removed. The announcement signal (US-1) and the email (US-3) come later and read what you build; they are not yours.
prior_decisions: decisions.md D2 — a removed publisher leaves a trace (publisher_subject), never a name or email (FR-014).
research.md R3 — account removal clears the FK through the plain base manager. Never set Meta.base_manager_name; T004 records a probe proving the test fails if you do (then revert).
decisions.md D4 — records.py (the personal-record answer) is NOT touched in this story; that question is with the maintainer.
docs/adr/0008 — the same two-identifier shape Acceptance uses (user + subject).
acceptance: publish(publisher=user) records the user on Version.publisher and str(user.pk) on Version.publisher_subject, via Acceptance.subject_of(); publish() with no publisher leaves both empty; a draft has neither, enforced by the widened check constraint.
Changing publisher/publisher_id/publisher_subject on a published version is refused by save() and by queryset update(), exactly like the wording.
Removing the publisher's account succeeds, leaves the version otherwise unchanged, clears publisher and keeps publisher_subject.

Version.publisher_display: None for a draft; str(publisher) when the account exists; 'An account since removed' when only the subject remains (never the subject itself); 'No publisher recorded' when both are empty.
Migration 0005 carries an existing published version forward with no publisher recorded.

The admin publish page records request.user as the publisher. Published by appears next to Published at on the version page and in the version and document lists, with query counts that do not grow with the row count.

CONTEXT.md defines Publisher; docs/models.md and docs/authoring.md describe the publisher, including their lists of what never changes; CHANGELOG [Unreleased] names the new personal data in plain language.
